content.title: About
content.content: Cooked celery consists of the stalks of Apium graveolens that have been peeled and boiled until tender. Cooking softens the characteristic crisp texture while retaining its distinctive aroma and adding a mild sweetness. It is used in soups, stews, salads, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Celery belongs to the Apiaceae family, the same as carrots and parsley.
It is very low in calories – about 16 kcal per 100 g of cooked product.
Ancient Romans used celery as a flavoring herb in many dishes.
While most people think of the stalks, celery roots are also edible.
Stalk color can range from light‑green to darker shades depending on the variety.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Celery provides flavonoids and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Its dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and overall gut health.

items.title: May lower blood pressure
items.content: Naturally occurring nitrates can help relax blood vessels.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Celery supplies potassium, magnesium and phosphorus, essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Practically fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to celery, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Celery contains oxalates, which in high amounts can contribute to kidney stone formation.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic celery, it is advisable to wash thoroughly and, if possible, peel before cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cooked celery as a side dish with meat, fish or poultry, add it to vegetable stews, soups and purees. It can be diced for salads with yogurt dressing or used in cold appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked celery in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
